messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Spanish, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | Ahi | An exclamation of emotional intensity. | Interjection **¡Ay!** (back‑translation: “Ah!”) | | quanto | Marks the degree of difficulty (“how hard”). | Degree adverb **cuán** (intensifier, not comparative) (back‑translation: “how”) | | a | Marks the infinitival complement of “tell”. | Preposition **a** introducing infinitive (back‑translation: “to”) | | dir | The act of expressing the unknown fact. | Infinitive verb **decir** (back‑translation: “tell”) | | qual | Introduces the content clause “what it was”. | Interrogative pronoun **qué** (head of embedded question) (back‑translation: “what”) | | era | Past state of the referent (the wood). | Imperfect indicative **era** (3ª sg.) (back‑translation: “was”) | | è | Present identification of the referent as a “thing”. | Present indicative **es** (3ª sg.) (back‑translation: “is”) | | cosa | The abstract entity whose description is difficult. | Noun **cosa** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “thing”) | | dura | Qualifies “thing” as difficult. | Predicate adjective **difícil** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “hard”) | | esta | Points to the specific wood being described. | Demonstrative adjective **esta** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “this”) | | selva | The forested area that is the subject of the description. | Noun **selva** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “wood/forest”) | | selvaggia | Attribute of the wood: untamed, natural. | Adjective **salvaje** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “wild”) | | e | Links successive adjectives. | Coordinating conjunction **y** (back‑translation: “and”) | | aspra | Attribute of the wood: physically harsh. | Adjective **áspera** (feminine, singular) (back‑translation: “rough”) | | e | Links successive adjectives. | Coordinating conjunction **y** (back‑translation: “and”) | | forte | Attribute of the wood: compact/solid. | Adjective **densa** (or **fuerte**) (feminine, singular); choose **densa** for “dense” (back‑translation: “dense/strong”) | | che | Refers back to “this wood”. | Relative pronoun **que** (introducing relative clause) (back‑translation: “which”) | | nel | Locates the mental action within “thought”. | Contraction **en el** (preposition + definite article) (back‑translation: “in the”) | | pensier | The mental representation of the wood. | Noun **pensamiento** (masculine, singular) (back‑translation: “thought”) | | rinova | Causes the fear to become fresh again. | Present indicative verb **renueva** (3ª sg.) (back‑translation: “renews”) | | la | Specifies the noun “fear”. | Definite article **el** (masculine, singular) because **miedo** is masculine (back‑translation: “the”) | | paura | The emotion that is re‑awakened. | Noun **miedo** (masculine, singular) (back‑translation: “fear”) |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Spanish components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 4: Ay cuan a decir qué era es cosa dura / Ay cuan a decir qué era es dura cosa / Ay cuan a decir qué era es cosa dura - Line 5: Esta selva salvaje y áspera y fuerte / Esta selva áspera y salvaje y fuerte / Esta selva fuerte y salvaje y áspera - Line 6: que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo / que en el pensamiento siempre renueva el miedo / que en el pensamiento constantemente renueva el miedo

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Spanish lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura Line Inventory: - Ay cuan a decir qué era es cosa dura Assembly Notes: - No additional function‑words or morphology needed; the phrase already contains the required infinitive marker “a”, the interrogative “qué”, the finite verb “es”, and the predicate “cosa dura”. Target Text: Ay cuan a decir qué era es cosa dura
Source Line: 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte Line Inventory: - Esta selva salvaje y áspera y fuerte Assembly Notes: - No extra words required; the phrase supplies the demonstrative, noun, and the three coordinated adjectives. Target Text: Esta selva salvaje y áspera y fuerte
Source Line: 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! Line Inventory: - que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo Assembly Notes: - Added the required exclamation at the end to match source punctuation; no other content added. Target Text: que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 4 - Target Text (from Step 4): Ay cuán a decir qué era es cosa dura - Back-Translation (literal): “Ah how to say what was is a hard thing” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what this wild and rough and dense wood was, … - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: Ay cuán es cosa dura a decir qué era
- Line #: 5 - Target Text (from Step 4): Esta selva salvaje y áspera y fuerte - Back-Translation (literal): “This forest wild and rough and strong” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): … what this wild and rough and dense wood was … - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 6 - Target Text (from Step 4): que en el pensamiento renueva el miedo! - Back-Translation (literal): “which in the thought renews the fear!” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): … which in thought renews the fear! - Checks: End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**UNVERIFIED** – failing lines: 4
